documents.title: Invitation to tender_Robocutting on Seafield and Strathspey Estates

lots.description:
The Cairngorms National Park Authority (‘the Park Authority’), on behalf of Seafield and Strathspey Estates, invites suitably qualified and experienced organisations to tender for 30 days of robocutting across three work areas within pinewoods around the villages of Boat of Garten and Carrbridge in the Cairngorms National Park.
 The gross work areas cover approximately 180 hectares of pinewood and bog woodland habitat. The contract is expected to achieve approximately 10–15 hectares of cutting within the work areas, based on an indicative rate of 2–3 hectares per week per machine. Actual output will depend on terrain and site complexity, which vary across the work areas. Site visits are encouraged to help tenderers assess ground conditions and submit an accurate bid. Tenderers must contact the Park Authority in advance to arrange access.

lots.description:
Clackmannanshire Council seeks to procure a cloud-based Data Governance Platform and associated services to provide enterprise-wide visibility, classification, and lifecycle management of information assets across its digital estate.
 The solution must be capable of securely connecting to and analysing data held across multiple systems, including on-premise shared drives, Microsoft 365 (SharePoint, OneDrive, Teams, and Outlook), legacy platforms such as Lotus Notes, and key line-of-business systems. It will be required to discover, index, and catalogue both structured and unstructured data, identify sensitive information (including personally identifiable information), and support the application of retention and disposal policies.
 The platform must also enhance the Authority’s ability to respond to statutory information requests by enabling efficient search, retrieval, review, redaction, and export of relevant data. In addition, it should provide risk insight, reporting, and automation capabilities to support ongoing data governance, reduce redundant and over-retained data, and improve compliance
 A detailed summary of requirements is included within the attached document

renewal.description: Renewal options will be permitted to support continuity of the SaaS service and avoid unnecessary disruption associated with changing data governance platforms. Any renewal will remain subject to satisfactory supplier performance, continued business need and the Council's procurement and budgetary requirements.

tender.title: Supply and Delivery of FPGA Based Configurable Multi-Instrument Source and Detector
tender.description:
Background
 The UK urgently requires a sovereign, open-access advanced semiconductor packaging capability to close a well-evidenced market failure. Today, UK innovators in photonics and power electronics rely on overseas Outsourced Semiconductor Assembly and Test (OSAT) facilities for scaling to volume packaging, which fragments the supply chain, extends lead times, increases Intellectual Property (IP) leakage risk, and exposes critical technologies to geopolitical disruption.
 The National Centre for Advanced Semiconductor Packaging (NCASP) is the missing link that converts research excellence into manufacturable products.
 NCASP is creating an integrated, industry-led scale-up facility that connects UK device design to domestic, high-volume packaging, test and metrology – reducing time-to-market and anchoring value onshore.
 Description
 University of Strathclyde has a requirement for a FPGA based configurable multi instrument source and detector.

tender.title: Tarbert Ferry Terminal to Whitehouse Active Travel Path Developed and Technical Design
tender.description:
This tender is for the Tarbert to Whitehouse Active Travel Path; linking the Tarbert Ferry Terminal (OS Grid NR871688) to the Kennacraig Ferry Terminal, Skipness Road End (B8001) and Whitehouse (OS Grid NR817613), and will build upon the concept design developed for the route (Connected Transport Planning, 2026).
 Argyll & Bute Council wish to appoint an appropriately qualified and experienced design team to develop the Tarbert to Whitehouse Active Travel Path project from the current concept design through Developed (RIBA Stage 3) and Technical (RIBA Stage 4) Design, and to be Principal Designer during construction (RIBA Stage 5).
 The project will require the successful tenderer to complete a range of survey, design and in-depth engagement work, including in-depth community, stakeholder and landowner engagement, topographic and utilities surveys and equality and socio-economic impact assessment (EqSEIA) to ensure route(s) identified have strong community, neighbour and landowner support and that the design drawings for the route(s) are robust, deliverable and of a high quality. These will all be subject to engagement with the community, businesses, landowners, neighbouring landowners, Argyll and Bute Council, CALMAC/CMAL, HITRANS and Transport Scotland.

lots.description:
The overall aim of this research is to provide information about the compensation received by those whose land is acquired under compulsory purchase powers. The evidence generated through the research is intended to inform decisions on potential future legislation by the Scottish Government and scrutiny of any such legislation by the Scottish Parliament.
 The objectives of the project are to address the following questions:
 a.	How frequently and to what extent are compensation payments affected by the prospect of future planning permission (“hope value”)?
 b.	In cases where hope value is a factor, to what extent are payments affected by the timing, costs and risks of implementing any such prospective planning permission?
 c.	To what extent does the current condition of property affect the market value calculated for the purpose of compensation?

 9. Terms and conditions covering all services set out for funeral directors and customers, including a clear disputes and resolution procedure if service quality is queried or challenged.

There is a minimum financial requirement that affects trading performance, and balance sheet strength.
 Financial requirements for trading performance and balance sheet strength should be calculated on latest filed accounts with Companies House.
 Trading Performance
 An overall positive outcome on pre-tax profits over a three-year period. Exceptional items can be excluded from the calculation.
 The above would be expressed in the ratio Pre-Tax Profit/Turnover.
 Balance Sheet strength
 Net worth of the organisation must be positive at the time of evaluation	 and organisation must not be subject to an insolvency process.
 Intangibles can be included for purposes of the Total Assets figure.
 The above would be expressed in the ratio Total Assets/Total Liabilities.
 If an organisation is only required to file abbreviated accounts with Companies House, then in the event of the organisation being successful in the procurement process, full set of accounts will be required in order to verify the above ratios have been complied with.
 An organisation should have no outstanding issues, with regard to statutory filing requirements with Companies House.
 Organisations who have been trading for less than the three years noted above must provide evidence that they are complying with the above minimum financial requirements for the period in which they have been trading.
 Organisations who do not comply with the above financial requirements but are part of a Group, can provide a Parent Guarantee if the Parent organisation satisfies the financial requirements stipulated above.

 Bidders are required to provide two examples delivered within the last three years which demonstrate your organisation’s relevant experience in providing specialist transportation services for fine art, museum objects, cultural collections, high-value fragile items, or equivalent sensitive goods.
 Bidders must ensure that the examples provided are relevant to the nature of this requirement and demonstrate suitable experience, capability and capacity to safely and securely transport fine art or comparable sensitive items.
 Your response must include, but is not limited to, the following:
 the name of the client or contracting authority, unless confidential;
 the nature and scope of the services provided;
 the type of items transported;
 the measures used to protect items during packing, handling, transportation, storage and delivery;
 any environmental, security, insurance, access or scheduling requirements managed as part of the contract;
 the contract value and duration, where this can be disclosed; and
 the outcome of the contract, including whether it was delivered to the required standard, timescale and budget.
 Summary: This requirement is intended to confirm that bidders have the necessary specialist approvals, secure premises, and operational controls to safely transport and, where required, store fine art and other sensitive cultural objects in accordance with the UK Government Indemnity Scheme. Responses must demonstrate that the bidder can meet the required security, environmental and transport standards for the duration of the contract.
 The evaluation of question one will be scored as per the Scoring Guidance.
 Question 2
 Bidders are required to confirm that their fine art transportation services are undertaken in compliance with the UK Government Indemnity Scheme: Transport Conditions and their storage premises are approved by the Manager of Security and Protection Advice, Arts Council England and comply with the UK Government Indemnity Scheme: Security and Environmental Conditions.
 Please provide details of when approval of premises was granted by the Manager of Security and Protection Advice, Arts Council England.
 The evaluation of question two will be scored on a pass/fail basis

tender.title: Helensburgh, Cardross, Dumbarton Cyclepath Active Travel Route - Phase 3: Developed & Technical Design
tender.description:
This tender is for Phase 3 of the Helensburgh, Cardross and Dumbarton Cyclepath; linking the Helensburgh Waterfront segregated cycleway (OS Grid NS 29598 82259) to the existing section of the cyclepath adjacent to the A814 at the Red Burn (OS Grid NS 31655 81112), near the north-east corner of Morrisons Supermarket site, and will build upon the concept design developed for the majority of the route (Civic Engineers, 2025).
 Argyll & Bute Council wish to appoint an appropriately qualified and experienced design team to develop Phase 3 of the Helensburgh, Cardross and Dumbarton Cyclepath project from the current concept design through Developed (RIBA Stage 3) and Technical (RIBA Stage 4) Design, and to be Principal Designer during construction (RIBA Stage 5).
 The project will require the successful tenderer to complete a range of survey, design and in-depth engagement work, including in-depth community, stakeholder and landowner engagement, topographic and utilities surveys, equality impact assessment (EqIA) and Preliminary Environmental Assessment (PEA) to ensure route(s) identified have strong community, neighbour and landowner support and that the design drawings for the route(s) are robust, deliverable and of a high quality. These will all be subject to engagement with the community, businesses, landowners, neighbouring landowners, Argyll and Bute Council, Strathclyde Partnership for Transport (SPT) and Transport Scotland.

 Ratios - a Pass in any two of the three ratios as an overall Pass for Economic and Financial standing.
 - (Ratio 1) Acid Test – (Current Assets-stock)/Current Liabilities. To pass the Acid Test Ratio question the bidder must have a score of greater than 1.
 - (Ratio 2) Return on Capital Employed %– Profit/Capital employed. To pass this question the Council require the bidder to score a positive figure/Percentage.

 WDC will use template WD09 - WDC Financial Vetting Questionnaire v1.0, it is recommended that candidates review their own ratio scores in advance of submitting their tender. tender.title: Caerlaverock Cluster-Wildlife and Natterjack Toad Pond Creation
tender.description:
We plan to create a mixture of Natterjack Toad ponds (designed to reintroduce historic breeding locations/habitat specifically for this species)
 (NJT Ponds) and more general habitat and water restoration ponds (HWR Ponds). The HWR ponds are designed to reinstate general habitat,
 but also to provide natural flood and surface water management, together with diffused pollution control and sediment catchment from
 adjacent hillside fields – acting as a buffer zone. In winter, the ponds will reach their maximum surface area, providing large waterways for
 migratory wildfowl. In spring the NJT ponds will reduce in size and leave a small deepening which will heat up quicker to trigger the Natterjack
 spawn. In summer they will provide habitat for damselflies and aquatic pond insects. We plan to create 24 ponds, totalling approximately
 22,000m2 across the estate adding to existing habitat and creating new wetland habitats. 7 will be natterjack toad specific ponds, and 17
 general habitat ponds. Rather than thinking of these ponds as individual assets, we have grouped them into pond networks by holding but also
 layering other wildlife restoration efforts nearby to maximise the ecological benefit for the habitat. The layout of each having been specifically
 designed to support whole ecosystems.

The data derived from the surveys and subsequent design work may be used by the landowner or their representatives for the purposes of Peatland Code registration. Protected species surveys are required to provide data to inform restoration design and identify potential ecological constraints.
 Detailed methodologies are provided for both survey types alongside this SOR.

tender.title: Flood Bank Realignment
tender.description: This collaborative project with SBAG address recurring concerns over beaver burrowing and floodbank breaches on high-value farmland along the River Isla, a major tributary of the River Tay (SAC). By realigning a floodbank and creating a wider more natural river corridor with willow buffer strip we intend to increase bank resilience, reduce beaver impacts and enhance biodiversity. Two participating agricultural landowners will trial setback embankments and habitat features including beaver mounds to encourage coexistence. The approach integrates agricultural resilience with river naturalisation, monitored by the river Restoration Centre and Beaver Trust to inform future coexistence strategies to promote biodiversity.
